neighbours.label: marking written text by circling, crossing out, underlining or striking through
fire: Ask your pupils to circle the verbs in each sentence.
Hand out the article and let them cross out every adjective.
Please underline the main idea in each paragraph of the essay.
The editor drew a strike through the last two lines of the draft.
On the worksheet, circle the correct answer with a pencil.
She read the contract and crossed out the clauses she disliked.
Have the class underline the rhyming words in the poem.
Use a red pen to circle any spelling mistakes in your notes.
quiet: Ask your pupils to copy the verbs from each sentence.
Hand out the article and let them read aloud every paragraph.
Please summarize the main idea in each paragraph of the essay.
The union called a strike over the last two years of pay.
On the playground, form a circle with the other children.
She read the contract and crossed the street to the bank.
Have the class recite the rhyming words in the poem.
Use a red pen to sign your name at the top of your notes.

notes: Card: ' circle' x4, ' cross' x2, '-decoration' x2, ' underline' x2, 'strike', ' Out'. Probe: ' through' after 'a strike' 1.489; ' in' after 'circle the two words' 0.674; ' out' after 'cross' 0.642; 'circle it in red' 0.491; 'read out' and 'say the two words' 0.008; 'sat in a circle' 0.005; 'cross the river' 0.056. Near misses keep the same words in another sense or the same frames with another verb.
